name: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk

frontmatter.title: DSSA: the parts, the upstream and the premium
frontmatter.summary: DSSA is a Sinar Mas conglomerate whose coal arm sits in a separately listed subsidiary. The parts are worth Rp233; the price is 3.6x that value. The konglo lens keeps only part of the premium over twelve months, giving a target of Rp518 and a SELL. The subsidiary's dividends reach the parent; the parent hoards them.
thesis: The parts — the listed coal stake at the covered subsidiary's house target, the non-coal segments at audited net book, the unallocated remainder, net of non-controlling interests and less a holding-company discount — are worth Rp233 after twelve months, far below the Rp750 price.
The own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped, not down-weighted: they are struck on the price history OJK found manipulated and sit several times above the parts.

The upstream is real: the parent receives its controlling share of the coal subsidiary's distributions. What never happens is a distribution from DSSA to its own shareholders, so the discount is a hoarding discount, not a dead channel.
Power and technology are fallback book marks, not house-card valuations; the report tests them and shows what a book haircut is worth.
The controlling shareholder has been fined over manipulation of trading in DSSA's own shares; the konglo lens slows the premium's compression rather than removing it.

catalysts.event: OJK hands the sanction letters over in person to the controlling shareholder and to nine exchange members
The regulator describes its market-conduct sanctions as the largest in its history and keeps criminal escalation open
IDX minimum free-float step takes effect for large caps; DSSA's free float clears the raised minimum but the group remains in the HSC regime
MSCI consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone status closes, with a decision due by 30 June 2027

blocks.text: **This revision removes the OJK-tainted multiples, corrects the upstream claim and re-rates the call from REDUCE to SELL.** The fundamental now rests entirely on the parts: the coal stake at the covered subsidiary's house target, the non-coal businesses at audited segment net book, plus the unallocated corporate remainder, net of the non-controlling interests that belong to outside holders and less a holding-company discount. That is Rp233 a share after twelve months, or Rp207 today [S0]. The price is Rp750, or 3.6x fundamental value [S0]. The konglo lens keeps part of that premium because a few per cent of the float sets the marginal price: the base regime case closes 45% of the log gap for Rp472, and probability-weighted across the three regime scenarios the target is Rp518, a -31.0% total return [S0]. The rating is SELL.

**Three corrections.** First, the own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped, not cut to a token weight: they are struck on the tape the regulator found was planned, structured and price-lifted [S10, S13, S14], and because they sat several times above the parts, even a ten per cent weight supplied about half the old fundamental. Second, the parent has received subsidiary dividends: the cash flow records the outside shareholders' share at USD 105 USD mm in FY2025 and USD 237 USD mm in FY2024 [S9], and the subsidiary's note records a total FY2024 distribution of USD 500 USD mm to all shareholders [S9]; at the 51.0% stake, the controlling share reaches DSSA and is reinvested. Third, the card's holdco deductions are applied: overhead capitalised at ten times the sourced office line, and a tested parent net-debt position [S9, F62].

**The variant view.** The market is not paying for the coal arm, which sits in a separately listed subsidiary valued at a fraction of the parent, nor for the non-coal parts at audited book. It is paying a 3.6x premium to the whole. The konglo lens explains why that premium can persist — thin float, index deletions and a live sanction — but it does not make the premium value. We mark the subsidiary at its house target, below its own quote, so the parts are not flattered by the market's optimism about the child [S0]. The nearest bull catalyst is not a first upstream from the subsidiary, which already happens, but a first distribution from DSSA to its own shareholders.

DSSA reports in US dollars and describes itself as an energy and infrastructure company [S9]. Revenue comes from four segments — captive steam and electricity, fertilizer and chemicals trading, coal mining and trading, and cable television, internet and technology, plus small renewable and other lines [S9].

Coal dominates: mining and trading revenue was 2,488 USD m against group revenue of 2,791.2 [S9, S0], behind the company's statement that mining is about nine-tenths of revenue [S3]. The coal business sits in PT Golden Energy Mines Tbk, listed since 2011, in which DSSA holds 51.0% directly [S9, S3]. The mines operate under coal contracts of work (CCoW), whose royalty and permit terms the group flags as a margin risk [S9]. The minority interest of 444.4 is largely the coal subsidiary's outside owners [S9].

The other pillars are smaller. Technology revenue was 212 USD m last year and 170 USD m in the first half, roughly double the prior period [S9, S6]; fertilizer and chemicals was 90.9 USD m; power has no external revenue because the fee is earned inside the group [S9]. The group says the energy pillar funds the build-out of the others, its stated reason for not paying a dividend [S6, S9].

Ownership is concentrated: PT Sinar Mas Tunggal holds 59.9%, insider holdings are 66.3% and the free float is 21.5% [S9, S0], and the controlling shareholder is the entity the regulator has just sanctioned [S10, S14]. Market capitalisation is 116,049,092,437,500.0 with about 427,113,583,150.8 traded a day, so no liquidity discount applies [S0]; the fifty-two week range of 432.0 to 4,640.0 shows the repricing [S0].

A listed parent that owns stakes in separately listed children usually trades at a discount to what
those stakes are worth: minority holders cannot direct the cash, cannot force a distribution, and bear
the cost of whatever the parent builds next. The discount narrows only when something specific and
dated forces value up to the parent.

DSSA is five businesses, and the house card says mark each on its own terms rather than apply a blanket multiple to the group [S9]. The largest is thermal coal. The coal price reaches DSSA through the listed subsidiary's own quote and house target, not through a mine model we build here, so the coal path enters the parts as the market's and the subsidiary's own view rather than a second, independent forecast [S9, S12].

Power is a captive processing fee with a large asset base and no external revenue [S9]. Chemicals is a low-margin distribution book [S9]. Digital infrastructure — broadband, homepasses and a data-centre build — is the fastest-growing revenue line [S6, S9]. Competitively, the group is a follower: the coal producer is mid-curve with a wide calorific range and a domestic, China and India customer mix [S9]; broadband and data centres face far larger incumbents in a scale business with front-loaded capital [S6, S9]; chemicals is a price-taker [S9]. Only the power processing agreement has a semblance of a moat, and it is the part with the largest book and the least external revenue [S9].

Two external influences matter: the market-conduct file against the controlling shareholder, which the house framework reads as a manipulation-class flag [S10, S14], and the coal royalty and permit regime, which the group flags as a margin risk [S9] and which reaches our target through the subsidiary's model.

Revenue fell to 2,791.2 last year from 3,017.8, and gross margin compressed to 33.7% from 40.7% [S0]. Net profit to the parent was 230.5, of which minorities took 130.7 [S0, S9], and return on equity was 16.0% [S9].

The data pack's depreciation is a fraction of the real charge because the cash-flow statement uses the direct method and carries no add-back; the segment note discloses consolidated D&A of 78.2 USD m and 83.6 USD m for the last two years, and the model carries that restated charge [S9]. Two splits make older per-share metrics not like-for-like [S0].

The forecast reproduces the last audited year's economics. Revenue growth of 10.0% takes the top line to 3,070.3, on the two plan numbers the company has disclosed: first-half technology revenue roughly doubled [S6, F20], and the coal subsidiary guides 58Mt of sales against the 56.7 MtMt it sold in 2025 [S12, F48]. Gross margin of 33.7% and EBITDA margin of 17.2% are held at last year's levels because no source supports a squeeze or a recovery [S0, S9], giving EBITDA of 527.0 and net profit to the parent of 164.3 [S0].

Capex of 513.7 against EBITDA of 527.0 leaves free cash flow to the firm of 38.6, and the same comparison was negative last year at -99.4 [S0]: spending absorbs essentially all the businesses generate, concentrated in the non-coal pillars [S9, S6]. We hold capex at last year's ratio without a source to change it [S0, S9].

The balance sheet carries cash of 575.5, debt of 1,486.2 and minorities of 444.4, for net debt of 910.6 and net debt to EBITDA of 1.9 [S0]. This is not charged twice: each part is valued after its own liabilities [S9]. The parent's bonds are inside the segment marks — segment liabilities of 2,121 USD m are within two per cent of consolidated liabilities (assets of 4,415 USD m less equity of 2,261 USD m) — so netting them again would double-count [S9]. The guarantees are a contingent claim in section six [S9].

**Earnings quality.** Accruals are negative in two of the last three years and marginally positive in the third: operating cash was 330 USD m, 693 USD m and 1,031 USD m against net profit of 361.2, 542.8 and 865.3 [S0, S9]. Cash covered profit in two of the three years and fell short by a whisker in the third, well inside the threshold. Free cash flow to the firm turns negative — -99.4, -139.4, 307.6 [S0] — a capital-spending story, not an accruals one. Technology assets grew from 1,162 USD m to 2,208 USD m in a year [S9]. Board status is main board, no special notation [S0]; the regulatory action is not a listing-status action on the issuer [S10, S14]. One sanctioned member is PT SS, whose director received an underwriter-licence freeze [S14, F57]; no DSSA entity or director is among the sanctioned parties, and the company says the matter does not affect its operations [S10, S11, S14].

Related-party purchases were 0.4% of cost of revenues and the related-party slice of G&A was 0.9%, mainly family property, telecom and insurance entities [S9]. The larger exposure is structural: allocating a data centre or broadband network between listed and unlisted vehicles is the family's choice [S9, S6], and the data-centre build already runs through a related party — KMG bought the package for the group's data-centre project from PT LG Sinarmas Technology Solutions for Rp1.2 Rp trntn [S9, F67].

**PSAK 16.** The power book does not carry a revaluation surplus today: the plants were sold in 2024, the decrease in the surplus was 160 USD m, the cumulative increment transferred to retained earnings was USD 111 USD mm, and the surplus line is nil [S9]. **Structure flags**: two splits, the restructuring that moved the subsidiary stake onto the parent's books, the elimination column of -1,954 USD m, and the treasury block of 1,516 million shares, 19.7% of issued capital [S9]. The disclosure items are optics-class; the regulator's finding that trading in DSSA's shares was planned, structured and price-lifting is manipulation-class, and it sits at the controlling shareholder rather than in the issuer's accounts [S10, S13, S14].

The house card values a holding company on its parts, less holdco net debt and a discount the base rate says persists [S0]. The parts carry 100% of the blend: the own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped because both sat several times above the parts and are struck on the tape OJK found manipulated [S0, S10, S13, S14]. The cost of equity is 12.4% and the weighted average cost of capital 10.8%, built in the table [S0].

**The parts.** Each mark is a listed price or an audited segment book; the bridge reconciles to consolidated equity and then cuts the consolidated total back to the parent's share. The coal stake is at the covered subsidiary's house target, not its quote, because the konglo card marks a covered listed subsidiary at its house target and that target sits below the market price [S0].

| Part | Mark | | --- | --- | | PT Golden Energy Mines Tbk, 51.0% stake | house target [S0, S9] | | Steam and electricity | net book, fallback [S9] | | Cable TV, internet and technology | net book, fallback [S9] | | Fertilizer and chemicals | net book [S9] | | Renewable energy | net book [S9] | | Other | net book [S9] | | Intra-group elimination | deduction [S9] | | Unallocated corporate and tax remainder | value [S9] | | Non-controlling interests | deduction [S9] |

Marks are assets less liabilities: 2,659 USD m less 668 USD m, 2,208 USD m less 1,114 USD m, 57.4 USD m less 32.6 USD m, 75.2 USD m less 1.0 USD m, 37.6 USD m less 0.6 USD m, the elimination -1,954 USD m less -197 USD m, and the remainder equity 2,261 USD m less segment net assets [S9].

**Power and technology are fallbacks, and tested.** Power has no external revenue and no segment result; its FY2024 comparative result was -0.2 [S9], so a fee business with no disclosed profit is at net book rather than an invented multiple. Technology has a segment result of 142 USD m, before operating expense; against net book of 2,208 USD m less 1,114 USD m that is about an eighth of book, and after the FY2024 comparative operating expense of USD 78.6 USD mm it is a mid-single-digit return, which does not prove the book [S9]. A ten per cent haircut would remove a material slice; the book is a floor with a range [S0, S9]. The PSAK 16 objection is answered: the plants were sold, the cumulative increment was transferred to retained earnings, and the surplus line is nil [S9, F49, F76].

**The reconciliation.** The segment books are stated in full; the parts must be the parent's share. Consolidated equity is 2,261 USD m [S9] and total non-controlling interests are 444 USD m [S9], of which the coal subsidiary accounts for 350 USD m [S9]. The coal segment's net book — 1,051 USD m less 502 USD m — is replaced by the parent's 51.0% share of the GEMS house target. GEMS's own net assets, implied by its 350 USD m NCI at the minority share (the complement of the 51.0% stake), are larger than that segment book, so the replacement strips the coal-column book but not the GEMS outside interest; the deduction line is the total non-controlling interest less the coal-column book the GEMS mark already removes beyond the parent's 51.0% share of GEMS's book. Read from consolidated equity, the bridge is 2,261 USD m, less the non-controlling-interest deduction, plus the difference between the GEMS house mark and the coal net book, equals the gross parts value before the holdco deduction [S9]. The elimination is inside the segment note, and because the bridge starts from consolidated equity, which already nets it once, there is no second elimination [S9]. The remainder is positive and in the base [S9]; half-year equity of 3,050 USD m is higher, though no interim segment note is in the register [S6, S9].

**The holdco bridge.** The parent's bonds and sukuk are inside segment liabilities — segment liabilities of 2,121 USD m are within two per cent of consolidated liabilities, and the Phase IV issue alone was Rp0.3 Rp trntn of bonds plus Rp1.2 Rp trntn of sukuk [S9, F68, F69] — so netting them again would double-count. What is not in the marks is parent overhead: the parent-level office expense of USD 3.9 USD mm [S9, F62], capitalised at ten times, is the deduction, a floor because the parent-only share of salaries is not published. The guarantees are a contingent claim in section six [S9, F63-F66].

**The upstream, corrected.** The old report said the parent had never received a dividend and the upstream-coverage ratio was zero. That was wrong. The cash flow records dividends to non-controlling interests of USD 105 USD mm in FY2025 and USD 237 USD mm in FY2024 [S9], and the subsidiary's note records total distributions of USD 500 USD mm for FY2024 and USD 500 USD mm for FY2023 to all shareholders [S9]. At the 51.0% stake the parent receives the controlling share; the outside line is the complement. That cash services the parent's bonds and funds the technology build. Against the capitalised office cost we deduct, the parent's share covers it about six and a half times on the FY2024 distribution and almost three times on FY2025 [S9, F58-F62]. The discount is therefore a hoarding discount — cash arrives at the parent and is not passed to its shareholders — not a discount for a dead channel.

**The discount.** A discount of twenty to forty per cent persists indefinitely, and a narrower discount needs a dated catalyst that upstreams cash [S0]. The one precedent is stale: a 2023 buyback took 484 USD m of stock off the market, of which 1,516 million shares, 19.7% of issued capital, still sits in treasury; part was reissued in 2024 for 48.9 USD m [S9]. The policy permits up to 30.0% of net profit and the parent has never paid a dividend [S9, S0]. We charge 30%, the middle of the persistent band, on the base rate and the non-enforcement structure — the related-party flow, the treasury overhang and the cross-guarantees [S9, F46-F67]; the stale buyback argues against the wide end, that structure against the tight end. The OJK trading sanction is not a second discount: the konglo card assigns it to the lens, and it is counted there once [S10, S14]. Even the tight end leaves the parts below the price [S0].

The sum of the parts is Rp207 a share; grown at the cost of equity for a year, with no dividend leg, that is the fundamental value of Rp233 [S0]. The price is Rp750, so the gap is the premium ratio of 3.6x, not the final target's expected return; the -31.0% figure is the return to the lens target only [S0].

**The konglo lens.** The engine measures the log premium of 1.3 [S0] and assumes only a share closes in twelve months because the marginal price is set by float: 21.5% of the capital trades [S9, S0]. The closing share is slowed by HSC listing, exit from the IHSG and the index family, and the live sanction [S15, S16, S10, S14], and is run over three regime scenarios, weighted (base at 50%): **bear** closes 85% of the gap for Rp282; **base** closes 45% for Rp472; **bull** closes none and the premium holds for Rp843 [S0]. Probability-weighted, the target is Rp518. We do not shade the parts toward or away from the market price [S0].

The grid is driven by the discount and the cost of equity and reports pre-lens values; it does not bracket the target because the lens adds most of the distance to the price [S0]. Section five shows the subsidiary's bear target effect instead.

On this method the target is set by the marked parts and the discount; the largest part is the subsidiary's house value, imported from its own model, so the grid shocks the discount and the two scenarios are discount scenarios in form [S0]. **Bear**: the governance file escalates, nothing is returned to DSSA holders, the coal marker normalises and the digital build consumes capital. The subsidiary already publishes a bear target; at that target the controlling stake is worth less than half its base mark, and the parent's fundamental value falls by about a quarter, while the lens cushions the twelve-month target [S0]. A ten per cent haircut to the two fallback book marks has a similar order of effect. **Bull**: a dated capital-allocation signal — a repeat buyback, a first distribution to DSSA holders or a stake sale — narrows the discount, with the 58Mt plan delivered and technology already doubling [S6, S9, S12]: a value of Rp237 and a target of Rp266, with base at 50% [S0]. Even at the subsidiary's own bull target the parent's lens target stays below the price: the largest component is a covered subsidiary's house target the parent does not control [S9].

**The konglo regime scenarios.** The lens reads the price at 3.6x fundamental value and asks how much of the 1.3 log gap the regime lets close [S0]. DSSA is on the HSC list and out of the IHSG from 2 November 2026 [S15, S16]; it was deleted from the MSCI Global Standard and FTSE Large Cap indexes in 2026 [S17, S18]; and the controlling shareholder carries an OJK sanction with criminal escalation open [S10, S13, S14]. The free float of 21.5% clears the raised minimum, so no forced supply step sits in the window [S0, S15]. The dated catalysts are the MSCI Standalone consultation, feedback closing on 30 April 2027 with a decision by 30 June 2027 [S6], the IDX free-float deadlines from 31 March 2027 [S15], and the enforcement file [S13]. The bear case is that the premium the lens keeps is what the 2026 regime is dismantling, so a faster unravel is a real risk.

Five risks carry weight. **Governance (high likelihood, high impact)**: the controlling shareholder has been fined over manipulation of DSSA's shares, exchange members were sanctioned, and criminal escalation stays open [S14, S10, S13]; we take the company at its word that operations are unaffected [S11] and still read it as a regime factor the konglo lens carries [S0]. **Capital allocation (high likelihood, high impact)**: capex absorbs essentially all of group EBITDA, the parent receives the subsidiary's distributions but passes none to its shareholders, and the equity has no yield support [S0, S9]. **Coal-market (medium likelihood, medium impact)**: the coal stake is marked at the subsidiary's house target, so a lower coal marker lowers the largest part directly [S9]. **Disclosure (high likelihood, medium impact)**: no segmental operating profit is published for the largest book-value segments; a technology-profit disclosure would be the biggest positive change [S9]. **Currency (medium likelihood, medium impact)**: the group reports in dollars, so the rupiah value of the parts moves with the exchange rate while the businesses do not [S0].
A dated action that distributes cash to DSSA's own shareholders — a dividend, buyback or stake sale — would justify a narrower discount [S9], while a criminal escalation widens it [S13, S10].

**The konglo profile.** DSSA is the Sinar Mas group's energy and infrastructure holding, the Widjaja family's listed vehicle and the parent of the separately listed coal miner [S9]. The controlling holding company holds 59.9% and insider holdings are 66.3%, leaving a free float of 21.5% [S9, S0]. That float clears the raised minimum [S0, S15], but DSSA is on the HSC list and out of the IHSG from 2 November 2026 [S15, S16], and was deleted from the MSCI Global Standard and FTSE Large Cap indexes in 2026 [S17, S18]. The live enforcement item is the OJK manipulation sanction against the controlling shareholder, the largest in the regulator's history and open to criminal escalation [S10, S13, S14]. The marginal price is set by a few per cent of the capital [S0].

**Structure flags.** Cross-guarantees: DSSA guarantees EMR facilities of Rp3.6 Rp trntn, Rp0.4 Rp trntn and Rp2.0 Rp trntn and the PT SMPlus data-centre facility of Rp0.4 Rp trntn [S9, F63-F66], contingent claims disclosed and not netted in the parts. Treasury: the 2023 buyback left 1,516 million shares, or 19.7% of issued capital, in treasury [S9, F46, F47] — potential supply and a governance overhang. Pledges: the report discloses pledges of GEMS-group shares and receivables for the subsidiary's bank facilities [S9, F74]; we found no disclosure of a pledge of the controlling shareholder's DSSA stake, a checked absence, not proof. Related-party assets: the data-centre build runs through PT LG Sinarmas Technology Solutions at Rp1.2 Rp trntn [S9, F67], and allocating assets between listed and unlisted vehicles is the family's choice [S9]. Each widens the warranted discount.

**Ownership and the sanction.** Minority holders have no practical influence over board composition or the decision to reinvest [S9]. The authority imposed an administrative fine of 1.5 Rp trn on the controlling shareholder over manipulation of DSSA's shares, found the manipulation planned and structured and price-lifting, sanctioned 9 exchange members and warned eight sales staff, and handed the letters over on 21 October [S10, S14]. It will escalate to a criminal investigation if the evidence supports one and calls the sanction the largest in its history [S13]. The company says the matter does not affect its operations or finances [S10, S11]; the market has not made that distinction [S0]. On the house framework this is a manipulation-class flag; the konglo card routes it to the regime lens, so it slows the premium's compression there and is not counted a second time in the holdco discount [S10, S11, S13, S14].

**Dividend and ESG.** The policy permits up to 30.0% of net profit [S9] and the parent has paid none to its own shareholders, on the company's stated explanation that its subsidiaries require the capital [S9]. The subsidiary does pay: the cash flow and its dividend note show distributions to all shareholders, of which the parent receives the controlling share [S9, F58-F61]. An upstream that arrives at the parent and stops there is the whole cost of the structure — a hoarding discount — and it is why the dividend-yield method is dropped [S0, S9]. On ESG the exposures are the ordinary ones for Indonesian thermal coal at the subsidiary, plus the governance sanction, on which this name would not pass a controlling-shareholder conduct screen today [S10], and a transition claim resting on disclosure too thin to underwrite [S9, S6].

Only the regulatory file and the index calendar carry dates. The sanction letters were handed over on 21 October to the controlling shareholder and exchange members [S14, S13]; whether the issuer faces action and whether the investigation reaches the courts is what sets the governance discount [S10, S11]. The HSC names leave the IHSG calculation from 2 November 2026 [S16], the IDX free-float step lands on 31 March 2027 [S15], and the MSCI Standalone consultation closes on 30 April 2027 with a decision by 30 June 2027 [S6]. The rest are undated watch items [S9].

The monitorables are method-specific. Any distribution from DSSA to its own shareholders — a dividend, buyback or stake sale — would attack the discount directly; the subsidiary's upstream already reaches the parent, so the missing leg is the parent's payout [S9]. Segmental operating profit and capital employed for technology, power and chemicals would let us mark those parts on their own cards instead of at fallback book [S9]. And who pays for the data centre and broadband build, at what return, is the item that would most change the parts valuation [S6, S9].

bear.narrative: The discount widens to the wide end of the persistent band: the governance file escalates to a criminal investigation, the group returns nothing upstream again, and the coal subsidiary's own quote carries the coal risk while the digital build keeps consuming capital. The subsidiary is itself a covered konglo name: its house target already blends its own bear, base and bull scenarios, and at its published bear target the 51% stake is worth less than half its base mark. The engine's SOTP mark is the subsidiary's probability-weighted house target, not a live coal model, so the scenario lever here is the discount; the report shows the coal-stake bear mark separately rather than pretending the engine re-prices GEMS.

bull.narrative: The discount narrows to the tight end of the persistent band on a capital-allocation signal we can see coming — a repeat of the 2023 holdco buyback, a first dividend, or a stake sale crystallising a mark [S9, F44] — with the coal subsidiary's 58Mt plan delivered [S12] and the digital pillar growing into its invested capital because technology revenue already roughly doubled in the first half [S6, F20], so the coal mark holds up and the discount narrows. Even here the parts do not reach the market's price.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

groups.name: Sinar Mas group (Widjaja family)
groups.role: energy and infrastructure holding company; parent of GEMS

enforcement.note: planned, structured trading manipulation of DSSA shares in 2023-2026 that pushed the price up; PT SMT fined Rp1.5tn, brokers fined and sales staff warned

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is anchored on the two plan numbers that ARE traceable and the last actual. The company's own target table carries revenue targets for FY2025 and FY2024 and gives no 2026 revenue number at all [S9, F15]. What the register DOES give for 2026 is the listed coal subsidiary's own plan — 58Mt of production and sales, above the 56.7Mt actually sold in 2025 [S12, F48, F1] — and the group's first-half technology revenue, roughly doubled year on year to USD 170.49m [S6, F20]. Coal is roughly nine-tenths of group revenue [S9, F7]. A full-year doubling of the USD 211.8m technology line [S9, F38] adds about eight per cent to the group, and the coal volume plan adds about two, which puts FY2026E about a tenth above FY2025A. That is a drift UP from the last actual that rests only on the two sourced plan numbers, not on a coal-price assumption. From FY2027E the first-half technology step is not extrapolated a second time and no source supports volume beyond the 2026 plan, so the top line fades toward the last actual rather than compounding; the fade feeds only the small earnings cross-checks and does not set the target, which is the sum of the parts.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Set at the last audited year's own gross margin (consolidated gross profit over revenue, FY2025A [S0, S9]) rather than the three-year average the starter carried, because the most-likely rule is that FY+1 reproduces the last actual year's economics and no source supports a further squeeze. The three-year average is flattered by FY2023, when the coal marker was roughly a third higher than it is today, so carrying it forward would import a peak-year margin into the forecast.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own ratio of SG&A and other operating expense to revenue [S0], held flat in real terms. The group's overhead carries the technology, chemicals and corporate functions as well as the mine, and nothing in the LK sources a step down; a decline would be an unsourced haircut.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set from the LK's OWN depreciation and amortisation, not the data pack's cash-flow feed: the group reports consolidated D&A of USD 78.2m for FY2025 and USD 83.6m for FY2024 in the segment note [F17, F18], roughly three times the pack's direct-method figure, and the ratio of that restated charge to revenue is what the forecast carries. The pack's D&A is small because the IDX cash-flow statement is prepared on the direct method and carries no add-back.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own ratio of capital spending to revenue [S0, S9], held flat. The group spends across the mine, the power assets, the broadband network and the data-centre build, and that spending absorbed essentially all of group EBITDA in the recent audited years; the ratio is the witnessed rate, not a target, and no source supports cutting it.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at the engine default (no new borrowing) with the caveat stated in the report rather than a fabricated financing plan: the LK says only that long-term bank borrowings may rise in the next few years to fund new projects and that the group funds capex from internal cash first, then short-term debt, then long-term debt, then new shares [S9], which is not a number we can date. On this method the forecast balance sheet feeds only the small earnings and book cross-checks, not the target, so an unsourced debt schedule would add false precision. Where the modelled cash path runs thin past the forecast horizon the report says so plainly [S9].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero, and sourced rather than assumed by omission: the group's policy permits a distribution of up to 30% of net profit [F14], but the accounts record no dividend payment in any reported year [S0, S9] and the company states it has not distributed dividends because its subsidiaries require substantial capital expenditure [S9]. A payout we cannot source, on a name that has never paid one, would be a fabricated leg in the blend; the engine therefore drops the yield method entirely.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The primary method is a sum of the parts with a holding-company discount, so no perpetual growth rate reaches the target; this input only frames the cross-checks. It is set at the house's long-run USD inflation assumption, below the house cap for a USD-reporting name, because a coal-heavy conglomerate should not be assigned perpetual real growth.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the house holdco archetype, not on a hope of narrowing: the base rate for holdco and SOTP names is that a discount of 20-40% persists indefinitely, and the recorded case file requires a NAMED, DATED catalyst that actually upstreams cash before a narrower discount can be underwritten. We hold 30%, the middle of that band. The stale end of the evidence argues against the wide end: this name has ONE capital-return precedent on the record — a holdco buyback of 154,105,327 shares in August-September 2023 for USD 483.8m, part of which was reissued to a third party in August 2024 [S9, F44, F45] — but it is three years old, has never been repeated, and the parent has never paid a dividend to its own holders [S0, S9]. The governance file argues against the tight end on its own merits and is NOT the OJK trading sanction: related-party purchases of family property, telecom and insurance, the data-centre package bought from a family affiliate, the treasury overhang and the cross-guarantees [S9, F46-F67] are the discount-widening structure. The OJK manipulation finding is assigned once, to the konglo lens (enforcement_manipulation), per the konglo card, and is not counted again here. The choice within the band is not load-bearing: the parts value is so far below the price that even the tight end leaves the bull leg below the market price.

challenges.challenge: The report states "no dividend has ever been received by the parent [S0, S9]" and "the upstream-coverage ratio is zero," but S9's consolidated cash flow records dividends of subsidiaries paid to non-controlling interests of USD 104,893,527 in FY2025 (line 51165) and USD 237,272,309 in FY2024, and GEMS's own notes record a US$500m final dividend for FY2024 plus interims to all shareholders (GEMS S3, p.89). DSSA's 51% share of those dividends is received by the parent and eliminated on consolidation; it funds the parent's own bond/sukuk service and the tech build. The load-bearing claim is untrue and no cited quote says what the report claims.
challenges.answer: Corrected in the model, facts and report. The parent does receive its controlling share of GEMS distributions: the consolidated cash flow records dividends to non-controlling interests of USD 104.893527m in FY2025 and USD 237.272309m in FY2024 [S9, F58, F59], and GEMS's note records total distributions of USD 500m for FY2024 and FY2023 to all shareholders [S9, F60, F61]. At the 51% direct stake the parent receives the complement of the NCI line; that cash services the parent's bonds and funds the tech build. The report now states the upstream and calls the discount a hoarding discount (cash reaches the parent and is not passed to DSSA holders), not a dead channel. Upstream coverage: the parent's 51% share of the FY2024 USD500m distribution is USD255m, about 6.6x the capitalised holdco office cost of USD38.79m; the smaller FY2025 distribution implies about USD109m to the parent, about 2.8x [S9, F58-F62].

challenges.challenge: The own-history P/E (18.98x) and P/BV (4.04x) multiples are explicitly described as struck on the price history OJK found manipulated, yet they contribute 680.5 x 0.10 = 68.0 and 985.7 x 0.10 = 98.6 USD m/share, i.e. 166.6 of the 335.6 blend (about half the fundamental), because their values are 3-4x the SOTP (222% and 367% above it). The 25%/15% -> 10%/10% reweight is cosmetic against that leverage, and the report calls them "small disclosed cross-checks" while they nearly double the value from the SOTP's 211 to 336.
challenges.answer: The own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped entirely, not down-weighted: valuation.weights are now SOTP 1.0, P/E 0.0, P/BV 0.0. The SOTP-only fundamental is Rp257 twelve-month (Rp228 today) and the konglo target is Rp534, versus Rp750, a -28.8% total return and SELL. The prior blend that gave the multiples 20% and produced Rp336/Rp611 is withdrawn. Engine now reports one method, the intended consequence of dropping the tainted series [S0, S10, S13, S14].

challenges.challenge: The steam/electricity part (assets F23 less liabilities F24 = USD 1,991m, 77% of gross parts) and the technology part (F25-F26 = USD 1,094m) are marked at 1.0x net segment book. That is a blanket book multiple applied to five segments, which the SOTP card forbids ("a bank sub via VAL_BANKS, a miner via VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL — never a blanket multiple"). No segment profit or EBITDA is disclosed, so neither mark is tested; the report itself concedes the power mark may be generous. The power book also carries a PSAK 16 revaluation surplus (F49 shows USD 160.2m derecognised on a power-plant sale), and the earnings-quality card requires pre-revaluation book value.
challenges.answer: Power and technology are now labelled fallback book marks, not house-card valuations, and are tested: technology has a disclosed segment result of USD 142.077674m [S9, F70] before its FY2024 comparative operating expense of USD 78.564274m [S9, F75]; against net book it is a mid-single-digit return after opex, which does not prove the book. Power has no external revenue and its FY2024 segment result was -USD 0.173519m [S9, F71], so a sourced EV/EBITDA multiple is not available without inventing one; it stays at net book with a stated range. A 10% haircut to both fallback marks gives SOTP v0 Rp188.6 and a lens target Rp502.4, still SELL. The PSAK 16 sub-claim is rebutted on evidence: the power plants were sold in 2024, the cumulative revaluation increment of USD 111.111816m was transferred to retained earnings [S9, F76], the decrease on sale was USD 160.2m [S9, F49], and the surplus line is nil at the last two year-ends, so the book is already post-revaluation and removing the surplus again would double-count.

challenges.challenge: The business scenarios are mirrored (+/-0.10 on a.holdco_discount) but never flex the largest value driver: the GEMS mark, which is itself priced off the coal deck, and the power/tech book marks. The bear narrative says "coal pressure / discount widens," yet the engine applies only the discount, so DSSA value under GEMS's own bear target (and under a tech/power book writedown) is never shown. GEMS's own konglo scenarios already produce a bear target; the parent report ignores it.
challenges.answer: The report now names the GEMS mark as the largest business lever and shows the parent at the subsidiary's own bear and bull targets in §5, with the numbers also stated here because the engine cannot re-price a covered subsidiary inside the parent SOTP. At GEMS's bear target (Rp2,360.6/share) the DSSA GEMS mark falls to about USD392.9m, DSSA SOTP v0 to Rp168.5 and the lens target to Rp485.3 (-35.3%). At GEMS's bull target (Rp11,404.9/share) DSSA SOTP v0 is Rp291.3 and the lens target Rp580.5, still below the Rp750 price. A 10% haircut to the two fallback book marks gives v0 Rp188.6 and target Rp502.4. The engine scenarios keep the mirrored +/-10pp holdco-discount shock because the SOTP mark is imported from GEMS's model, not a live line; the report discloses that limitation rather than pretending the grid captures it [S0, S12, F48].

challenges.challenge: Two card-mandated holdco deductions are missing. Holdco opex capitalised at ~10x is not computed (the report lists it as a missing output), and holdco_net_debt is set to 0.0 by assertion. The parent demonstrably issues its own debt — Shelf Bonds I Phase IV 2025 Rp256.7bn plus Sukuk Rp1,243.3bn (S9) — and gives corporate guarantees for subsidiary facilities, so "zero by assertion" is an unsourced optimism that raises the SOTP by whatever parent-level cost and guarantee risk exists.
challenges.answer: Holdco overhead is now capitalised and deducted: office expense USD 3.878624m x 10 = USD 38.78624m, set in valuation.holdco_net_debt [S9, F62]. Parent net debt is zero on a sourced reconciliation, not assertion: the parent's own Shelf Bonds/Sukuk (Phase IV alone Rp256.7bn bonds plus Rp1,243.3bn sukuk [F68, F69]) are liabilities of the Company, and segment liabilities of USD 2,120.892479m [F43] are within 1.5% of consolidated liabilities (USD 4,414.950126m assets less USD 2,261.2m equity = USD 2,153.75m) [F41, F51], so the parent debt is inside a segment mark and netting it again would double-count. Guarantees (EMR Rp3.6tn, Rp420bn, Rp2.0tn; PT SMPlus Rp400bn) are disclosed as contingent claims in §6 [F63-F66], not netted as debt.

challenges.challenge: The konglo profile omits structure flags the cards require: cross-guarantees (DSSA guarantor for EMR Rp3.6tn, Rp2.0tn, Rp420bn and PT SMPlus Rp400bn facilities, S9), the 19.68% treasury overhang as potential supply (F46/F47), a stated check (or absence) of pledged controlling shares, and the related-party allocation of data-centre/broadband assets between listed and private vehicles. Any of these widens the warranted discount under the governance rule.
challenges.answer: The konglo profile now carries each flag with a source: cross-guarantees for EMR facilities of Rp3.6tn, Rp420bn and Rp2.0tn and PT SMPlus Rp400bn [S9, F63-F66]; the 19.68% treasury block of 1,516,238,270 shares as potential supply [S9, F46, F47]; a stated pledge check - the report discloses pledges of GEMS-group shares and receivables for subsidiary facilities [S9, F74], and no disclosure of a pledge of the controlling shareholder's DSSA stake was found, stated as a checked absence; and the related-party SMX data-centre package from PT LG Sinarmas Technology Solutions at Rp1.22672802tn [S9, F67]. The bear/discount discussion now says these widen the warranted discount and keep it away from the tight end.

challenges.challenge: The intra-group elimination column (-1,953.5 assets / -196.5 liabilities, net -1,757) is sized against a segment note in which coal still appears at book. In the SOTP the coal segment is replaced by GEMS's standalone house value (which already nets GEMS's own intercompany payables), while the full consolidated elimination is still deducted. Because the coal/non-coal split of the -1,953.5 intercompany assets is not disclosed, the SOTP may double-deduct intercompany balances between GEMS and its siblings.
challenges.answer: The double-count is removed by construction. The SOTP now starts from consolidated equity of USD 2,261.2m [F41], replaces the coal segment's net book (USD 1,050.656086m assets less USD 502.007387m liabilities [F72, F73]) with the GEMS house value, and adds the unallocated remainder (equity less segment net assets, [F42, F43]). The elimination column is inside the segment note; because the bridge starts from consolidated equity, which already nets it once, there is no second elimination. The reconciliation is shown line by line in §4 and the parts table now includes the unallocated remainder.

challenges.challenge: The konglo-profile facts are cited to company sources that do not contain them. The MSCI Global Standard and FTSE Large Cap deletions are cited [S10, S11], which are the Kompas and detik OJK- sanction articles with zero MSCI/FTSE text; the HSC listing and 21.46% free float are cited [S3, S4], which are the mining web page and a detik FY2024 results piece with no HSC, IHSG, LQ45 or free-float text. The citations appear to borrow the konglo deck's S-numbering, which differs from the company's fund record.
challenges.answer: Every konglo citation is re-pointed. HSC listing and the IHSG exclusion are now cited to S15 (detik HSC list, 82 issuers, 22 Oct 2026) and S16 (Fortune IDN, HSC names out of the IHSG from 2 November 2026), archived in fund record. The MSCI Global Standard deletion is cited to S17 (Investortrust, May 2026 review) and the FTSE Large Cap deletion to S18 (Investortrust, June 2026 rebalance). Free float is cited to S0/IDX-IC, and the konglo registry (asof 2026-10-27) was used for group/HSC status. The old [S3]/[S4]/[S10]/[S11] konglo citations are removed from those claims.

challenges.challenge: §4 renders "that blend is the fundamental twelve-month value of Rp377 a share ... and it sits -18.6% below the price." Rp377 against the Rp750 price is -49.7%; -18.6% is the final Rp611 target's total return. The sentence confuses the fundamental gap with the post-lens expected return and understates by about 31pp the premium the konglo lens is priced on.
challenges.answer: The sentence is corrected: the report now states the fundamental gap as the price/fundamental premium ratio of 3.3x (Rp750 against Rp228 today; Rp257 twelve-month fundamental), and keeps -28.8% only for the final lens target's total return. The -18.6% claim is gone [S0].

challenges.challenge: The non-coal marks use FY2025 audited segment book, but group equity rose to USD 3,050m at H1-2026 (F21) from USD 2,261m at FY2025A (F41), and the segment-net versus total-equity residual (2,013.47 vs 2,261.20, about USD 248m) is disclosed as positive but never allocated. The report says the direction is up but quantifies neither, so a genuine upside to the parts is stated only in words.
challenges.answer: The unallocated corporate and tax remainder is now a base holding row, not a one-line acknowledgement: USD 247.729687m, the difference between consolidated equity of USD 2,261.2m [F41] and segment net assets (USD 4,134.362792m assets less USD 2,120.892479m liabilities) [F42, F43]. The H1-2026 equity of USD 3,050m [F21] is noted as directionally higher but not rolled into the audited segment books because no interim segment note is in the register.

challenges.challenge: The sensitivity grid is driven by holdco_discount and COE and reports pre-lens values of Rp347-408, while the published target is Rp611 because the konglo lens adds about Rp234. A reader told to "read the answer off the grid" cannot (it does not bracket the target), and the lens parameters that create most of the target (compress shares, regime probabilities) are not sensitised at all.
challenges.answer: The sensitivity grid is labelled pre-lens and the report states it does not bracket the target because the konglo lens adds most of the distance to the price. §5 now gives the regime scenarios (bear/base/bull with their targets) and the GEMS bear/bull overlay; no reader is told to read the answer off the grid [S0].

challenges.challenge: The bull case does not credit the one part with a sourced growth fact: technology revenue roughly doubled to USD 170.49m in H1-2026 from USD 87.15m (F20, S6), faster than any other pillar, while GEMS has guided 2026 production and sales to 58Mt above its 2025 actual (F48, S12). Both are archived but neither is allowed to lift the bull: tech is held at stale FY2025 book and the bull moves only the discount. The report's own §5 says a technology-profit disclosure would be the biggest positive change, yet the bull does not value even the revenue it can already see.
challenges.answer: The bull case now credits technology revenue roughly doubling to USD 170.49m in H1-2026 [S6, F20] and GEMS's 58Mt plan [S12, F48], and §5 states that even at GEMS's own bull target the DSSA lens target is Rp580.5, below the Rp750 price. Technology stays at fallback book because no segment capital/return disclosure supports a higher mark; the report says a technology-profit disclosure would be the biggest positive change.

challenges.challenge: The coal licence class that governs the GEMS mark is never stated in the DSSA report, contrary to the desk directive to state the licence: the group's mines operate under PKP2B CCoWs (BORNEO CCoW 007/PK/PTBA-BI/1994, BSL 015/PK/PTBA-BL/1994, GEMS card/S9). Separately, the group model carries no deck driver (drivers_used {}), so the FY2027E-30E -5%/-6% revenue fade is hand-set rather than engine-linked to the Newcastle deck path.
challenges.answer: The CCoW licence class is now stated in §1 (coal contracts of work) and the royalty/permit regime is described in §2, with the margin-risk disclosure cited [S9]. The FY2027-30 revenue fade remains a calibrated accounting path for the small earnings cross-checks only: the model carries no deck price driver (params empty), the report no longer claims deck linkage for the fade, and the target is SOTP-driven, so the fade does not set the rating. A full deck-linked revenue path is left for the next refresh when the template supports a price driver.

missing_bull_case.note: The recurring cash upstream from GEMS to DSSA is omitted. S9's consolidated cash flow shows "dividends of subsidiaries paid to non-controlling interests" of USD 104,893,527 (FY2025) and USD 237,272,309 (FY2024) [S9], and GEMS's own notes record a US$500m final plus interims paid to all shareholders in 2023-2025 [GEMS S3] — so the 51% controlling share reaches DSSA every year and is reinvested, not absent. The report instead asserts "no dividend has ever been received by the parent" and a zero upstream-coverage ratio (§4), which removes the most honest holdco-quality metric and the nearest bull catalyst.

missing_bear_case.note: Structure and contingent claims are understated: DSSA gives corporate guarantees for subsidiary loans (EMR Rp3.6tn/Rp2.0tn/Rp420bn; PT SMPlus Rp400bn, S9), the 19.68% treasury stake is potential supply (F46/F47), and the konglo card's pledged-share check is neither done nor stated. The bear narrative names coal pressure but the engine shocks only a.holdco_discount +0.10, so a coal fall through the GEMS mark — the largest part — is never in the numbers.

assumption_realism.note: The two largest non-coal marks, power (USD 1,991m, 77% of gross parts) and technology (USD 1,094m), are both 1.0x net segment book — a blanket book multiple across five segments that the SOTP card forbids ("never a blanket multiple"); no segment profit or EBITDA is disclosed to test them. FY2026E +10% revenue is traceable to GEMS 58Mt and doubling tech revenue [S12, S6], but the FY2027E-30E -5%/-6% fade is asserted off "nine-tenths coal" with no line-by-line bridge. Holdco net debt 0.0 and zero holdco opex are asserted, not sourced.

evidence_and_citations.note: Load-bearing failures, not nits. (1) "No dividend has ever been received by the parent" / "upstream ratio is zero" is contradicted by S9's NCI-dividend lines and GEMS's dividend notes. (2) The MSCI Global Standard and FTSE Large Cap deletions are cited [S10, S11], but those company sources are OJK-sanction articles with zero MSCI/FTSE mentions; the HSC listing and free-float facts are cited [S3, S4], which are the mining web page and a detik results piece and contain no HSC, IHSG, LQ45 or free-float text. The konglo registry (coverage/universe/konglo.yaml) is the authority and must be cited, or the deck sources added to fund record. (3) §4 renders "Rp377 ... sits -18.6% below the price"; Rp377 vs Rp750 is -49.7% (-18.6% is the 611 target's return). Spot-checks that do verify: F16 (OJK Rp1.5tn, S10), F35 (GEMS 51%, S9), F42/F43 segment totals, F17/F18 D&A, F52 OCF, F44/F45 buyback.

valuation_method_fit.note: The SOTP frame and the GEMS house mark are correct per card (GEMS marked at tp_final 6,763, below its 7,375 quote — conservative). But the method is only half applied: the two own-history multiples (18.98x P/E, 4.04x P/BV), which the analyst itself says are struck on the OJK-manipulated tape, still supply 68.0 + 98.6 = 166.6 of the 335.6 fundamental (about half) despite the 10%+10% weights, because their values are 3-4x the SOTP; the reweight is cosmetic against that leverage. Holdco opex at ~10x cash is required by the card and omitted; holdco net debt is 0.0 by assertion although the parent issues its own bonds/sukuk (S9); the -1,757 net intra-group elimination is sized against a segment note that still contains coal at book while coal is replaced by GEMS's standalone value, so the intercompany split must be shown. The konglo lens parameters are not sensitised: the published grid (347-408) is pre-lens.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose claims "the fundamental work is unchanged" and calls the multiples "small disclosed cross-checks," yet they nearly double the fundamental (211 -> 336) and lift the lens target from roughly 476 to 611 — half the answer rests on a series the report calls sanctioned conduct. The -18.6% fundamental-gap misstatement (§4) understates the premium. Credit where due: the rating survives the stress test — doubling the regime-bear probability (50/25/25) gives about Rp570, still below the Rp750 price — and the scenario shocks are mirrored (+/-0.10 discount).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The group model carries no deck driver (drivers_used {}, params {}), so the coal path reaches the target only through GEMS's own model; the FY2027E-30E -5%/-6% revenue fade is hand-set, not engine-linked to the Newcastle deck path, and should be shown as the deck's mean reversion or removed. The coal licence class that governs the GEMS mark (PKP2B CCoWs for BORNEO/BSL, S9/GEMS card) is never stated in the DSSA report, contrary to the desk directive to state the licence. Thermal-coal NEUTRAL tilt and USD reporting are consistent.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservatism (below last actual / unsourced down): non-coal marks use FY2025 audited book while group equity rose to USD 3,050m at H1-2026 (F21) from 2,261m (F41); the positive unallocated segment remainder (~USD 248m) is disclosed but not allocated; FY2027-30 revenue fade. Optimism (raises value): holdco opex capitalisation omitted; holdco net debt 0.0 with parent bonds and cross-guarantees; power carried at book without removing the PSAK 16 revaluation surplus (F49 USD 160.2m). Payout zero and capex/gross-margin at last actual are sourced and correct.

calibration.note: fund record qc passes with zero BLOCK flags; calibration ebitda_margin FY2025A actual 0.171645 vs model 0.171643 (gap -0.00017pp); both WARN flags (weights.changed, konglo.overlay) are justified in qc_justifications. Caveat: because params carry no price/volume driver, the calibration is a margin identity and does not re-price FY+1 at last-year benchmarks, so it does not validate the FY2027-30 revenue drift.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. SELL, target Rp518 (-31.0%) reproduces: fundamental Rp207 today / Rp233 twelve-month, price 3.62x value, konglo lens base closes 45% of the log gap (Rp472), bear 85% (Rp282), bull 0% (Rp843), probability-weighted Rp518. Konglo read passes: section 4 explains the lens, section 5 carries the business and regime scenarios separately, section 6 gives the profile, and the regime catalysts are dated (OJK letters 21-24 Oct 2026; HSC/IHSG exit 2 Nov 2026; free-float step 31 Mar 2027; MSCI consultation 30 Apr 2027, decision 30 Jun 2027). HSC and the manipulation enforcement are counted once, in the lens (+0.05/+0.10), not again in the 30% holdco discount. Group consistency: GEMS is marked method house at its approved target Rp6,763 (its HOLD, below the Rp7,375 quote), not at market; the upstream is corrected (parent receives the 51% share, covering the capitalised office cost ~6.5x on FY2024 and ~2.9x on FY2025); no intra-group deal omitted; the regime reading matches GEMS's own note. NCI bridge verified: gross parts USD2,578.5m = consolidated equity 2,261.2 less NCI 259.6 plus the GEMS-mark-over-coal-book increment 576.95; the USD1,125.6m GEMS mark is 51% x Rp6,763. Most-likely standard: business scenarios are mirrored (+/-0.10 on the discount; 25/50/25, base 50%), GEMS bear/bull are tested separately in section 5, and the base carries no default haircut (30% is the mid of the persistent 20-40% band). Q9's 1.0x-book fallbacks on power/technology (77% of gross parts) and Q8's unsourced FY2027-30 fade are disclosed; the fade feeds only the zero-weighted cross-checks, and a 10% book haircut still leaves the probability-weighted target far below Rp750, so neither breaks the SELL. Publication conditions (prose only; no number changes): (1) the investment summary says the call "re-rates from REDUCE to SELL" - the prior published call (approved 2026-10-27, Rp387) and history v1-v3 are all SELL, so it must read "maintains SELL and lifts the target from Rp387"; (2) FIX Q7 is still visible in the render ("USD 105 USD mm", "Rp1.2 Rp trntn"); (3) NOTE Q10 remains (H1-2026 equity 3,050 [S6] vs the pack's 2,093.9). Clear Q7, Q8, Q10 and the REDUCE line before the next version. Contamination: the KB index entry coverage:DSSA.JK carries a stale summary ending "REDUCE" while its rating field is SELL; that artifact is the likely source of the report's REDUCE line and must be corrected at the KB index (I do not edit it), not in the model.

bias.note: Round 2. The round-1 too_bullish driver (USD444.4m of NCI left inside the per-share value) is resolved and the SELL survives. The bridge now reconciles to the parent's share: gross parts USD2,578.5m, not USD2,838.2m, = consolidated equity 2,261.2 less the NCI deduction 259.6175 plus the GEMS-mark-over-coal-book increment 576.95. The closing share is slowed by live regime flags — HSC listing and exit from the IHSG [S15, S16], MSCI and FTSE deletions [S17, S18] — and by the OJK manipulation sanction on the controlling shareholder [S10, S13, S14]. The OJK finding is counted once, here in the lens, and not again in the holdco discount. The lens and its regime scenarios are explained in the report's §4 and §5, not bent toward or away from the market price [S0]. No consensus input is used.
